QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_25

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (open-ended, monthly dealing, equalisation accounting) had HWM NAV/unit of INR 1,200. Current NAV/unit is INR 1,260 (above HWM). A new investor subscribes at INR 1,260. To ensure fairness across unit-holders, what must the fund do?

answer.text: Charge the new investor an equalisation CREDIT on the INR 60 gain above HWM
Charge the new investor an equalisation DEBIT because they enter above HWM
Refund the incentive-fee accrual to the new investor
Reset the HWM to INR 1,260 for the entire unit class

explanation.text: The Logic: Equalisation accounting is used by open-ended hedge-fund-style vehicles to keep incentive-fee fairness across investors who subscribe at different NAV points relative to the HWM. When a new investor enters ABOVE the HWM, they have not participated in the gain from HWM to current NAV — without correction they would pay incentive fees on a gain that pre-existed their entry. The standard remedy is an equalisation CREDIT to that investor (reflecting the incentive-fee accrual they should not bear). An equalisation DEBIT applies in the mirror case of entry BELOW HWM. Resetting HWM for the entire class is not the answer because it would dilute legacy investors. The Trap: B swaps credit and debit relative to the entry-above-HWM scenario. C mis-describes the mechanism as a refund of accrued incentive fees. D resets HWM class-wide, which would transfer value from legacy investors to the manager. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (102, 112, 142, 350) support fund-administrator role, redemption mechanics, HWM, and NAV disclosure, but do not describe equalisation credit/debit accounting for subscriptions above HWM. The framing above is general industry/accounting practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
